reader.notes: The file-name tier is emitted first and each case returns, so a mode USE can never run for a named file. COBOL0897's message cites §2023 at --std 85, a citation-label nit outside this rule.

refuter.evidence: r1_prec.cob (r1_prec-001): the container R1OUT has USE GLOBAL ... ON GF (GF is an FD IS GLOBAL file) and contained R1C has USE ... ON INPUT. C's READ of GF (open INPUT, key absent) printed C-INPUT then C RESUMED 23: the compiler ran C's mode declarative for a file another USE names explicitly. GR4 read literally ('no other USE statement applies to file-name-1') and GR5b's own exception ('except those files referenced by file-name-1 in another USE statement specifying the same condition') both say C's INPUT declarative does not apply to GF, so it does not qualify and X.5.5.4 GR1b selects OUTER-GF-NAMED. The compiler's reading is that GR4/GR5b reach only USE statements of the same Procedure Division (as the corrected SR3 is scoped: 'within the same Procedure Division') and X.5.5.4 GR1a then picks C's own declarative first. The 1985 text does not settle which. Within one program the reader's verdict holds: every single-program probe and r5_named.cob (r5_named-001: named USE runs for 47/48/46 and no mode USE exists) agree. cite.py: 'OK  §1985:IX.4.8.4 GR4  (4.8.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR4' for 'no other USE statement applies to file-name-1'; 'OK  §1985:IX.4.8.4 GR5b  (4.8.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR5b' for 'except those files referenced by file-name-1 in another USE statement specifying the same condition'; 'OK  §1985:X.5.5.4 GR1a  (║5.5.4 General Rules║)  the text is in GR1a' for 'The declarative within the program that contains the statement which caused the qualifying condition'; 'OK  §1985:IX.4.8.3 SR3  (4.8.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR3'. No kb/Work note found (grep 'USE GLOBAL.{0,120}(file-name|named)').
refuter.corrected: Undecided between two readings: if GR4 binds across programs, C-INPUT is wrong (expected OUTER-GF-NAMED 23) and the verdict is non-conforming (wrong-answer, cause b: UseTierEmitter.EmitScopeTiers selects the program's own tiers before the GLOBAL walk at every edition). If GR4 is scoped to its own Procedure Division, CONFORMS stands.

adjudication.reason: A contained program's own USE ON INPUT runs, not the container's USE GLOBAL ON the file (kb/Work PB5812). Decided by the 1985 text: §1985:IX.4.8.3 SR3, word for word the same as §1985:VII.4.6.3 SR3, scope the USE statements to one Procedure Division, so GR4 and GR5b speak of one Procedure Division's statements, and §1985:X.5.5.4 GR1 orders the programs (the contained program's own declarative first).
